items.title: Data: Same Song, Dollars Up And Donors Down
items.summary: New Fundraising Effectiveness Project data show donation dollars rose 6.6% in the second quarter of 2026 compared with 2025, while the number of donors fell 1.6% year over year so far this year.

items.title: A new tax credit could change where education donors give
items.summary: A 2025 tax provision creates a tax credit of up to $1,700 for donations to qualified scholarship granting organizations, beginning January 1, 2027. The IRS released initial rules, but questions remain about how these organizations will work with schools and whether the credit will reduce other giving.

items.title: Anthropic’s $300 billion promise leaves nonprofit leaders asking who decides and when
items.summary: Anthropic plans to put 5 percent of its shares into an LLC, the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, subject to shareholder approval. Its seven co-founders have pledged to donate 80 percent of their shares to philanthropic causes, though the filing says that pledge is not binding. The company says these moves plus an employee matching program will send roughly 20 percent of shares to the public good.

items.title: Budget 2026: pension pots removed from IHT charitable giving rules
items.summary: UK Budget 2026 removes pension pots from inheritance tax charitable giving rules, according to Business & Accountancy Daily.

items.title: Ford Foundation Unveils 7-Point Funding Realignment
items.summary: The Ford Foundation unveiled a new strategic direction focused on the preconditions for democracies to thrive, including protecting democratic values, fundamental freedoms, and inclusive economies worldwide. The article describes a seven-point funding realignment.

items.title: Veteran charities are highly visible but get less than 1 percent of U.S. giving
items.summary: Donations to military and veteran charities rose 5.9 percent in 2024 to about $4 billion, before inflation adjustment, according to Indiana University's Lilly Family School of Philanthropy. The top 10 recipients captured 85 percent of that growth. Their share of U.S. giving was 0.68 percent in 2024 and has stayed between 0.6 and 0.7 percent for a decade.

items.title: Further Scaling Our Malaria Grantmaking
items.summary: GiveWell expects to grant more than $1 billion this year, more than double the $418 million committed in 2025. It aims to grant at least $2.5 billion in new malaria funding from 2027 through 2032, potentially several times that. Possible recipients include the Against Malaria Foundation and Malaria Consortium, along with new organizations and funding vehicles.

items.title: National Philanthropic Trust Launches "Building the Next Era of Philanthropy" Initiative as New Donors Reshape Charitable Giving
items.summary: National Philanthropic Trust has launched a "Building the Next Era of Philanthropy" initiative, framed around new donors reshaping charitable giving.

items.title: A grant isn’t always the right tool: The case for program-related investments
items.summary: An article argues that foundations underuse program-related investments, which let them deploy loans, equity, and other repayable capital for charitable purposes. It says only a small fraction of foundations use them.

items.title: Who gets to decide who decides? The power problem inside participatory grantmaking
items.summary: An article examines how authority is distributed in participatory grantmaking, distinguishing funders who consult communities from those who cede decision-making power. It draws on the Participatory Grantmaking Community definition and Arnstein's ladder of participation.

items.title: Who’s paying to protect democracy? Meet the 10 biggest donors.
items.summary: A Chronicle tally shows that $266.5 million of $369.2 million in $1 million-plus gifts to democracy programs since 2006 was given from 2021 through 2025. Universities received most of these gifts, and the largest was $59 million to USC.

items.title: Big money is flooding elections, and grant makers have walked away
items.summary: A Pew Research survey found Americans rank money in politics as a very big problem, above inflation and health care affordability. A Philanthropy for Active Civic Engagement survey of its members found grant makers ranked money in politics/corruption last among 13 democracy issues.

items.title: What happens when a fiscal sponsor shuts down?
items.summary: The High Desert Community Foundation will end its fiscal sponsorship program on December 31, 2026, affecting more than 30 community projects. Operations are expected to cease by the end of June 2027, and sponsored projects must find independent status or a new sponsor.

items.title: Study: First Time Donors Found Via Social Channels

items.title: The New Nonprofit Visibility Gap (Blog)

items.title: Money worries cloud voter mobilization efforts
items.summary: The Voter Participation Center ran a $40 million midterm turnout campaign after funding arrived late in the summer. The group, which has 501(c)(3) and 501(c)(4) arms, aims to help 500,000 people register and 400,000 apply for vote-by-mail. Its past funders include donor-advised funds and the MacArthur Foundation.

items.title: Why direct mail still delivers at year-end in the age of AI
items.summary: The National Park Foundation's direct mail revenue rose from $17.4 million in 2024 to $28.25 million in the fiscal year ended September 30, more than half its $48.7 million annual giving. Its leaders said AI did not drive that growth. Other fundraisers describe direct mail's continued effectiveness.
